In exchange, Chevron will transfer its interests in offshore Plataforma Deltana Block 2 and Block 3 gas licenses and its non-operated interest in the Petroindependiente joint venture to PDVSA.

The article highlights each company's unique strengths, such as ExxonMobil's dividend stability, Chevron's production momentum, and ConocoPhillips's earnings sensitivity to rising oil prices, while noting that a drop in oil prices to the low $60s is the primary risk for all three.
feed.title: The 3 Best Energy Stocks to Invest $1,000 in As Oil Hits $100 A Barrel

feed.summary: Toyota is reportedly developing a high-performance off-road variant of its Tundra pickup, potentially named the "TRD Hammer," to directly compete with the Ford F-150 Raptor. This comes after Toyota filed a trademark for the name and an anonymous insider confirmed a more capable Tundra is in the works, featuring 37-inch tires, long-travel suspension, and a high-output powertrain. Meanwhile, General Motors is noted for its absence in this specific desert-runner segment, despite offering other off-road capable trucks.
feed.title: Toyota Tundra TRD Hammer Could Rival F-150 Raptor, But Where Are You GM?

feed.summary: Texas Pacific Land (NYSE:TPL) is reportedly shifting its focus to AI-focused data center infrastructure and power generation projects on its extensive land in the Permian Basin, moving beyond its traditional oil, gas, and water services. feed.title: Texas Pacific Land Explores AI Data Centers As New Revenue Stream

feed.summary: Eni, the Italian energy major, has announced plans to increase its distribution policy to shareholders and launch a share buyback program worth at least 1.5 billion euros ($1.72 billion) over the current year. The company aims to return between 35% and 45% of its operating cash flow to shareholders and will also reduce investment spending, boost oil-and-gas production, and dilute its stake in its renewable power and electric-vehicle charging unit as part of its new strategy through 2030. Investment firm Ares is expected to contribute at least 1 billion euros to a capital increase related to these changes.
feed.title: Eni Increases Distribution Policy, Launches $1.72 Billion Buyback

feed.summary: Colorado energy regulators have approved a $1.5 million fine against Chevron for the largest well blowout in the state in a decade. The fine, with about $1 million dedicated to buttressing statewide enforcement programs, comes after the Bishop well incident in April 2025, which released 25,000 barrels of material and prompted evacuations. While regulators deemed the settlement "tough but fair," some environmental groups argue it does not adequately cover the damages inflicted on the community.
feed.title: Chevron’s $1.5M fine for Weld County blowout will finance improvements to monitoring programs
